strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy PR #21335 at buggy commit 87ed0cab1a60: build scipy from source, then run the developer's new TestCauchy tests (cdf/sf/ppf/isf against mpmath references, rtol=1e-15). On the buggy revision, ppf(0.5) returns -6.123233995736766e-17 where the test demands exactly 0.0, so test_ppf_isf fails. On the fixed revision the Boost-backed scu._cauchy_ppf/_cauchy_isf give exact zero and the test passes. The transition depends on the in-tree Boost build and the x86_64 Linux double-precision toolchain, not on printed values.

build_commands: git clone https://github.com/scipy/scipy.git && cd scipy && git checkout 87ed0cab1a60 && git submodule update --init
pip install -r requirements/build.txt (or the equivalent pip install of the build deps listed above)
pip install -e . --no-build-isolation (or python dev.py build) so the compiled extension is built from the buggy revision's in-tree Boost headers
git apply the PR test diff to scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py and scipy/stats/tests/test_continuous_basic.py
pinned_because: numpy<=2.0: era ceiling from PR date 2024-08-08 (era-inferred, not documented; chosen because it was the newest release at that date)
scipy 1.14-era build deps: era-inferred, not documented; the buggy revision builds against its own requirements files
boost: no documented constraint and no era entry; choose the copy vendored in-tree at 87ed0cab1a60 (the one the PR's scu wrappers compile against) and say so explicitly; do not install a system Boost

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py::TestCauchy::test_ppf_isf (parametrised p=0.50 expects ref 0.0) and TestCauchy::test_cdf_sf; secondary: test_continuous_basic.py cauchy entry (fails_cmplx change)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 87ed0cab1a60 with the PR test diff applied, TestCauchy::test_ppf_isf[ppf-p=0.50] (and likely some test_cdf_sf tail cases) FAILS because assert_allclose(-6.123233995736766e-17, 0.0, rtol=1e-15) has atol=0 and cannot pass. On the PR head (fixed revision), the same selection PASSES: all TestCauchy cases match mpmath references at rtol=1e-15 and ppf(0.5) is exactly 0.0.
strategy.numerical_probe: cauchy.ppf(0.5) compared against exact 0.0 with atol=0
risks: Needs an in-tree build of the buggy commit; the defect is only observable when the compiled code and Python layer match that revision, so reuse of an older wheel will not reproduce it.

The defect is double-precision IEEE arithmetic; no sanitizer, fast-math, or non-x86 platform is stated by the evidence, so the transition is assumed only on standard x86_64 Linux. On other architectures or with -ffast-math the exact-zero comparison may behave differently.
Boost version is unbounded in the evidence; a different Boost than the vendored copy could change the fixed-revision result, so use the in-tree copy.
The test_cdf_sf cases at extreme tails (x=+/-5e15) depend on the arctan2 rewrite; the buggy revision may or may not fail there, so the defining failure should be taken from test_ppf_isf at p=0.5.
The fixed-revision pass for p=0.25 relies on the PR discussion claim of one-ulp accuracy, not an independent check here.
Subnormal input 5e-324 overflow behaviour is discussed in the PR but is not exercised by this test; do not add it to the success criterion.

The fails_cmplx edit in test_continuous_basic.py changes which tests are expected to fail for complex arguments; if the test file is applied differently, the secondary selection can change without affecting TestCauchy.

oracle.tolerance: rtol=1e-15, atol=0 (assert_allclose); exact 0.0 required at p=0.5
oracle.reference_source: mpmath, per the comment in the test diff
oracle.why: The test compares against mpmath references with rtol only, so the zero reference at p=0.5 demands exact zero.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy 87ed0cab1a60, ppf(0.5) returns -6.123233995736766e-17; assert_allclose against 0.0 with atol=0 sees a nonzero difference and raises AssertionError, so test_ppf_isf for p=0.50 fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the PR head, scu._cauchy_ppf(0.5, 0, 1) returns exactly 0.0 and the other TestCauchy references match within rtol=1e-15 per the PR discussion, so the selected tests pass.
